title: mine ADDR_CANON_COMMON for US
headline: Do NOT extend ADDR_CANON_COMMON for the US. It already fires on 15,139,578 of 54,780,019 pooled US address tokens (27.637%), and 7,036,251 of the 7,331,972 non-identity rewrites (95.97%) land on a canonical value that is itself a live token, i.e. genuinely fuse. The measured upside ceiling is 295,721 = 0.5398% of listed mass (eleven keys that rename a US token onto a canonical value occurring ZERO times in the corpus), against an already-realised Class-A blocking cost of 3,150,695 = 5.7517% plus 309,855 = 0.5656% deletion.

dictionaries_as_built.source: _upstream/src/normalize.py and keys.py, parsed directly out of the source text

class_A_blocking_destroyed.condition: key NOT in ADDR_GENERIC but canonical value IS in ADDR_GENERIC

class_B_blocking_created.condition: key IS in ADDR_GENERIC but canonical value is NOT

fusing_vs_rename_to_dead.definition_fusing: canonical value occurs one or more times in the US union
fusing_vs_rename_to_dead.definition_rename_to_dead: canonical value occurs ZERO times in the US union, so the mapping cannot bring two observed surface forms together

subsplit_no_sibling_key.members: heights->hts, mountain->mtn, junction->jct, industrial->indl, plaza->plz, freeway->fwy, expressway->expy
subsplit_no_sibling_key.note: pure one-way renames, no other table key maps to the same dead target

subsplit_sibling_key_also_dead.note: sibling keys exist in the table but that target is also dead in the corpus, so observable fusion is still zero

empty_mappings_us.correction: 15 is correct; the work order's 13 is off by two
empty_mappings_us.verdict: harmless for the US, and the 'null' deletion is LOAD-BEARING: normalize.py:329 only skips a component whose stripped text is exactly null/<null>/n/a/na/none, so these 283911 come from 'null' embedded in longer text that the :329 guard does not catch

state_skip_union_bound.method: replicated normalize.py:333-335 over the 104 runtime US_STATES keys, summing addr_tokens.US occurrences
state_skip_union_bound.caveat: build_profile.py:126-127 flattens components, so this is an UPPER BOUND on rows, not a row count

wy_collision.fix_location: normalize.py:333 positional logic, NOT a dictionary entry

new_defect_saint.status: CONFIRMED defect, fix DEFERRED, no dictionary change recommended
new_defect_saint.statement: saint is UNMAPPED in ADDR_CANON_COMMON while st->st (street); NAME_CANON:131 and ADDR_CANON_FR:207 both map st->saint
new_defect_saint.why_no_fix_recommended: saint in US addresses is more often part of a CITY name (St Louis, St Paul) than a street name, so saint->st would fuse two genuinely different concepts and fire on every occurrence. Needs component-position awareness, which this profile cannot express.
new_defect_saint.mirror_of: D120's France wrong-sense finding, running the other way: the US is WITHHELD a needed sense

mirror_risk_clean.statement: all non-US-sense keys fire zero times in the US union; UK/India spelling variants are all 'not in the top 4000'

extension_candidates.mechanism: clean: township is NOT in ADDR_GENERIC, so no Class-A blocking loss
needs component position, not a dictionary
fixes D083 D2 plus the dead-token finding
Class A: estate IS in ADDR_GENERIC, net unclear
boro/bo not in top 4000, would create a dead token

extension_total_if_1_3_5_7.note: optimistic sum counting overlapping concepts once, before any Class-A blocking loss is deducted, versus an existing 5.7517% Class-A cost

unhandled_us_tokens_by_type.note: TOKEN OCCURRENCES. Every zero means 'not in the top 4000 of the six profiles', never 'does not occur'. Type labels are inferences from token identity; counts are measured.

gaps: IDF effect not computable: features.py:13-20 uses idf=ln(n/df) where df counts ROWS containing a token after list.unique(), but addr_tokens gives token OCCURRENCES, flattened and truncated to 4000. No IDF-shift number is estimated anywhere in this report.
No component structure: build_profile.py:126-127 flattens on [,;] boundaries. This is why the state figure is a union bound and why the saint defect cannot be fixed from this evidence.
Top-4000 truncation on all six addr_tokens.US lists; union is 4510 distinct tokens. Every absent/zero means not in the top 4000.
Hapax pruning at build_profile.py:26 and 45-48 drops count<=1 tokens, so listed mass under-counts by an unknown amount.

Tokenizer mismatch: build_profile.py:28 TOKEN_RE [a-z0-9]+ runs WITHOUT strip_accents, while normalize.py:317 calls strip_accents first. Small effect for the US (D120 measured 71.9x more impact for France) but short-token US claims are lower bounds.
Leetspeak in US addresses unmeasured and out of scope: normalize_address :314-353 never calls translate(LEET); only _name_tokens :280 does. The fleet's 24hr/1st findings are a name-path defect.
No row-level effects measured. atoks traced into prep.py:16 -> features.py:98,112,123-124,129 and keys.py:39,41-43, but score movement is not quantified.
method: Python broken on this box; all computation in PowerShell. ADDR_CANON_COMMON parsed by regex over _upstream/src/normalize.py:153-198 (177 entries, matching D083). ADDR_GENERIC parsed from keys.py:14-19. US_STATES parsed from normalize.py:216-229 and the runtime self-map loop at :251-253 replicated. Token counts summed across all six analysis_out/profile/*.json addr_tokens.US. No raw TSV opened, no network, _upstream/ and the dataset untouched.
